limitations: Most recordings come from sleep clinics: people referred for suspected sleep disorders, not the general population.
The external test set (UCDDB) has only 25 nights, so every number has a wide confidence interval.
The MIT-BIH training data come from 16 subjects, all male.
Accuracy on home wearables (watches, chest straps, rings) has not been validated; all heartbeats here were detected from clinical ECG.
The 3-stage (wake / NREM / REM) and 4-stage (wake / light / deep / REM) results are experimental and agree with the reference less well than sleep/wake.

Apnea definitions differ: Apnea-ECG comes with its own expert per-minute apnea labels, while UCDDB minutes are derived here from scored apnea and hypopnea events, so external apnea numbers mix model error with definition mismatch.
The apnea output is a screening hint, not a diagnosis. Only a sleep study read by a clinician can diagnose sleep apnea.

v2.note: UCDDB is a second look: v1 was already evaluated on it. HMC is the untouched v2 test set.

exclusion_rule.text: Primary analysis: recordings where fewer than 50% of the 30-second epochs have enough usable heartbeats are left out (pre-registered in docs/v2_protocol.md). All-records analysis: every recording.

rule.tie: accepted candidates within 0.01 kappa of the best -> fewest of {ensemble, smoothing, extra features, class weighting}; then higher kappa
rule.multiclass: the chosen spec is also the 3- and 4-class model (no separate choice)

rule.metric: cross_dataset.mean.kappa_pooled (minute kappa; fold A apnea-ecg -> slpdb, fold B slpdb -> apnea-ecg)
rule.tie: within 0.01 kappa -> fewest of {ensemble, class weighting, extra features, slpdb in training}
rule.note: Cross-dataset folds do not depend on train_on (each side is one database), so candidates differing only in train_on tie there; train_on is read from subject_cv_union.

limitations: Most recordings come from sleep clinics: people referred for suspected sleep disorders, not the general population.

v2 was chosen on training data only (cross-dataset tests between CAP and MIT-BIH, and between Apnea-ECG and MIT-BIH for apnea), frozen, and then tested once on 151 HMC recordings that had never been used. 5 HMC recordings with too little usable heartbeat data are left out of the primary analysis.
UCDDB (25 nights) is a second look for v2: v1 had already been evaluated on it, so its v2 numbers are less independent than the HMC numbers.
v2 agrees better with the sleep lab epoch by epoch, but its total sleep time and sleep efficiency errors are not smaller than v1's.
Wake-bout counts are not reliable: v2 counts fewer wake bouts than the sleep lab, and on UCDDB its wake-bout error is larger than v1's.
Suspected apnea minutes are still evaluated only on UCDDB; HMC was not used for apnea.
Accuracy on home wearables (watches, chest straps, rings) has not been validated; all heartbeats here were detected from clinical ECG.
The 3-stage (wake / NREM / REM) and 4-stage (wake / light / deep / REM) results are experimental and agree with the reference less well than sleep/wake.

Apnea definitions differ: Apnea-ECG comes with its own expert per-minute apnea labels, while UCDDB minutes are derived here from scored apnea and hypopnea events, so external apnea numbers mix model error with definition mismatch.
The apnea output is a screening hint, not a diagnosis. Only a sleep study read by a clinician can diagnose sleep apnea.
